title: The sheaf condition on a basis may be checked on a cofinal system of coverings
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology and satisfies $U\cap V\in\mathcal B$ for all $U,V\in\mathcal B$. A *$\mathcal B$-covering* of $U\in\mathcal B$ is a family $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of members of $\mathcal B$ (any index set $I$, possibly empty) with $\bigcup_iU_i=U$; a $\mathcal B$-covering $(V_j)_{j\in J}$ of $U$ *refines* $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ if there is a map $\alpha:J\to I$ with $V_j\subseteq U_{\alpha(j)}$ for all $j$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of sets on $\mathcal B$: sets $\mathcal F(U)$ for $U\in\mathcal B$ and maps $s\mapsto s|_V:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal F(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B$, with $s|_U=s$ and $(s|_V)|_W=s|_W$. Say that $\mathcal F$ satisfies the *gluing condition* for a $\mathcal B$-covering $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of $U$ if for every family $s_i\in\mathcal F(U_i)$ with $s_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=s_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}$ for all $i,j\in I$ there is exactly one $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ with $s|_{U_i}=s_i$ for all $i$. Suppose that for every $U\in\mathcal B$ a set $C(U)$ of $\mathcal B$-coverings of $U$ is given which is *cofinal*: every $\mathcal B$-covering of $U$ is refined by some member of $C(U)$. If $\mathcal F$ satisfies the gluing condition for every member of $C(U)$, for every $U\in\mathcal B$, then $\mathcal F$ satisfies the gluing condition for every $\mathcal B$-covering of every $U\in\mathcal B$. (Example: if every $\mathcal B$-covering of every $U\in\mathcal B$ is refined by a finite one, $C(U)$ may be the set of finite $\mathcal B$-coverings of $U$, including the empty covering of $U=\emptyset$.)
